column1: # How people actually type Bengali in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Chat spelling drops vowels wholesale ("tmr" for তোমার, "amk" for আমাকে), and
# no phonetic rule recovers a vowel that was never typed, so those spellings
# are listed outright. Colloquial and regional inflections ("boltiso" →
# বলতিসো) are here for the same reason.
# Derived from the romanized Bengali frequency list in wmkeyboard-data
# (data/bn/bn_rom.txt.gz), limited to spellings seen 5+ times. The 2000
# most frequent entries were reviewed a second time.
# Added after those, and some first readings changed: spellings from BanglaTLit's
# seen in 2+ posts and read by hand. Rebuilt by wmkeyboard-data's
# scripts/mine_bn_spellings.py, whose lists hold what was left out and why.
# Format: spelling<TAB>bengali   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
# Loaded after en_bn.tsv, so the hand-written loanword spellings win a tie.
# Hand edits here are welcome and outrank everything the generator produced.
# Reph spelled with one r. Avro's rules only write reph for "rr", so "dhormo"
# alone reads ধরম; these are the reph words of the bundled dictionary as
# people spell them with a single r, so they still type as they should.
# Generated from app/dictionaries-src/bn.txt through BengaliRomanizer, keeping
# only spellings the rules miss, that are not English words, whose rule
# reading is not itself a common word, and that the romanized corpus does not
# use for something else (parsi is পারছি, not পার্সি).
# ঙ before a vowel sign. The rules write ঙ্গ there, as desktop Avro does, since
# it is the commoner spelling (সঙ্গে, জঙ্গল); these are the everyday words
# spelled with a bare ঙ instead, where the bundled dictionary ranks that form
# at least twice as high as its ঙ্গ twin. Capital "Ng" types a bare ঙ anywhere.
# Vowels left out. Chat spelling drops a word's vowels mid-word ("klke" for
# কালকে, "lgbe" for লাগবে), and no rule can put back what was never typed.
# Mined from the romanized corpus: each spelling here is seen 5+ times, is
# read as no word by the rules, the siblings or the rest of this list, and
# reduces from fuller spellings in the corpus that almost all mean the same
# word. Hand-checked; ambiguous ones (parlm: পারলাম or পড়লাম) are left out.
